chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) move his lips when he intended to go out, while he was standing at the door. So I said, 'I saw you moving your lips when you went out. Did you say anything?' He said, 'Yes.'

Indeed, when a person exits from his house, he should say when he intends to go out: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest' three times. 'By Allah I exit, and by Allah I enter, and upon Allah I rely' three times.

'O Allah, open up goodness for me in this direction of mine, and end it for me with goodness, and protect me from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on the Straight Path.'
He would remain in the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah returns him to the place from which he came.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific litany of dhikr and supplication to be recited while standing at the threshold, highlighting the transition from the private sphere to the public as a moment requiring divine safeguarding. The emphasis on 'Bil-Lahi akhruj' (I exit by Allah's leave) and 'Al-Lahi atawakkal' (I rely on Allah) underscores the Shia theological principle of integrating immediate reliance on God with practical action, ensuring the believer remains under Allah's protection until their safe return.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub AL Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza who said,

‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> move his<sup>asws</sup> lips when he<sup>asws</sup> wanted to go out, and he<sup>asws</sup> was standing at the door. So I said, ‘I saw you<sup>asws</sup> moving your<sup>asws</sup> lips when you<sup>asws</sup> came out. So did you<sup>asws</sup> say anything?’ He<sup>asws</sup>: ‘Yes.

The person, when he wants to go out from his house should say when he intends to go out, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest!’, three times. ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I exit, and by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I enter, and upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> I rely’, three times.

‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Open up goodness for me in this direction of mine and Save me from the evil of every animal You<sup>azwj</sup> Seize by its forelock. My Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is on the Straight Path’,
would not cease to be in the Guarantee of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Returns him to the place which he was in’.
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from abu Hamza who has said the following:

“Once I saw abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) moving his lips when he wanted to go out of his house while standing at the door. I said, ‘I saw you at the door moving your lips when coming out, did you say something?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes,

when a man is leaving his home he should say, “Allah is greater than can be described, [three times], by the help of Allah I come out and by the help of Allah I enter and in Allah I place my trust, [three times].
O Lord, open to me this with goodness and finish it with goodness, protect me against the evil of every moving thing on earth that You keep in Your control. My Lord is on the right path,”
he will continue to be under the protection of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, until He brings him back to the place where he was before.’”
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub from abu Hamza has narrated a similar Hadith.
